correctness.rationale: Every minimally spectral order-four groupoid is either constant, one-input permutation, or Latin by counting solutions of xy=xz and yx=zx. A one-input permutation has only the identity or one-fixed-point/three-cycle type by the xx=x constraint; all five types satisfy every equation. The finite exact verifier exhaustively enumerates 576 Latin squares, applies four necessary equations, finds 30 surviving labeled tables in five simultaneous-isomorphism orbits, and certifies equality of their canonical set with five explicit affine F4 tables. Every binary term in each affine representative is an F4-linear form, so every equation is always true or has solution probability 1/4. The 22 non-Latin labeled and 30 Latin labeled tables prove the totals.

originality.rationale: Theorem 3.8 in Cardó 2026 supplies the known quasigroup/isocyclic reduction, while Section 6 lists five nonquasigroups and only the Klein-four quasigroup for order four and states that other examples were not found. The four further affine F4 quasigroup classes and the complete ten-isotype/52-labeled census are not implied by the printed six examples, nor by a mere classification of Latin squares. Exhaustive direct equivalence and domination searches in the accessible research record and primary sources found no earlier matching full claim. This is a qualified novelty judgment, not a uniqueness guarantee.
